title: Israel Police disable internal systems over fear of leaking sensitive information; cause unconfirmed
date_note: Ynet's page shows no publication day; Arab48 (23 November) relays it. Both say the incident began on Sunday; the day used is the day of the report.
summary: Ynet reports that Israel Police deliberately took several internal systems offline, including the Misseronet messaging system, as a precaution against information leaks after what authorities called a "complex technological incident" that began on Sunday. Investigators are examining a possible cyberattack, and an external technical malfunction has not been ruled out. About 100,000 police personnel must reset their passwords.
plain: Ynet says Israeli police switched off internal systems on purpose to prevent leaks. It is not known whether it was an attack or a fault. About 100,000 personnel must reset passwords.
exec: Ynet reports a national police force took internal systems offline as a precaution; the cause is not established.
geo_basis: national police force; the article names no city (point placed at Jerusalem)

evidence.quote: approximately 100,000 police personnel will be required to reset their passwords for internal systems.

validation.note: Ynet's original was read (via a fetch sub-agent, no publication day shown) and Arab48 relays it, so one publisher; the police statement is quoted by Ynet, no direct police page read.

review.note: evidence quote was not word for word; replaced with Ynet's exact sentence. Rest matches Ynet and Arab48; Ynet shows no publication day so it is left unset
